notes: CDER API-manufacturer CGMP letter for a peptide (GLP-1) API repackager/relabeler: inadequate QU oversight of unapproved suppliers, relabeling/repackaging without documentation and with altered manufacturing/retest dates, no process or cleaning validation, inadequate analytical method validation, inadequate water-system monitoring, and drug-listing/misbranding violations for mislabeling the true manufacturer of two semaglutide batches (both voluntarily recalled). Products named in clear are the drug substances 'semaglutide' and 'tirzepatide'; is_sterile_product is false because the letter explicitly frames these as non-sterile APIs intended for later use in sterile injectable drug products. organisms lists 'Pseudomonas aeruginosa' and 'Bacillus subtilis', which appear only in the context of inconsistent microbial-limit-test validation data (duplicated/missing results), not as confirmed contamination in distributed product -- flagged as a borderline reading of the organisms field. Did not add data_integrity or unapproved_new_drug to violation_categories: the letter does not cite a record-falsification/data-integrity regulation or a 505 unapproved-new-drug charge specifically; the closest issues (undocumented date changes, supplier mislabeling) are captured under misbranding/CGMP/adulteration instead -- judgment call.
